extracted.intended_audience: State environmental agencies, EPA regional offices, and owners/operators of electric generating units (EGUs) responsible for compliance with CAA section 111(d) emission guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and compliance criteria for State plans and affected EGUs under the EPA emission guidelines (Subparts TTTTa and UUUUb) including recordkeeping, monitoring, definitions, emission standards, and State plan content and approval procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator testing and conditional approval of CO2 storage technology
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator may test the system, or require the applicant to perform any tests considered by the Administrator to be necessary to show the technology's effectiveness, safety, and ability to store captured CO2 without release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator may grant conditional approval of a technology, with approval conditioned on monitoring and reporting of operations, and may withdraw approval on evidence of releases of CO2 or other pollutants. The Administrator will provide public notice of any application and of any proposed action on a petition before final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: General recordkeeping requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must maintain records of the information you used to demonstrate compliance with this subpart as specified in § 60.7(b) and (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for affected EGUs subject to the Acid Rain Program
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs subject to the Acid Rain Program, you must follow the applicable recordkeeping requirements and maintain records as required under subpart F of part 75 of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum recordkeeping for affected EGUs not subject to Acid Rain Program
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs that are not subject to the Acid Rain Program, you must follow the recordkeeping requirements in subpart F of part 75 to the extent those records provide applicable data for compliance determinations; at a minimum, specified records must be kept as applicable to the continuous monitoring systems used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum required records include: (i) monitoring plan records under 40 CFR 75.53(g) & (h); (ii) operating parameter records under 40 CFR 75.57(b)(1)-(4); (iii) records under 40 CFR 75.57(c)(2) for stack gas volumetric flow rate; (iv) records under 40 CFR 75.57(c)(3) for continuous moisture monitoring systems; (v) records under 40 CFR 75.57(e)(1) (except (e)(1)(x)) for CO2 concentration monitoring systems or O2 monitors used to calculate CO2 concentration; (vi) records under 40 CFR 75.58(c)(1) (specific paragraphs) for oil flow meters; (vii) records under 40 CFR 75.58(c)(4) (specific paragraphs) for gas flow meters; (viii) quality-assurance records under 40 CFR 75.59(a) (paragraphs (a)(1)–(12) and (15)) for CEMS; (ix) quality-assurance records under 40 CFR 75.59(a) (paragraphs (b)(1)–(4)) for fuel flow meters; and (x) DAHS verification records under 40 CFR 75.59(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of hourly and total CO2 mass emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep records of the calculations you performed to determine the hourly and total CO2 mass emissions (tons) for each operating month and each compliance period, including each 12-operating-month compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of gross or net energy output calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with § 60.5520a, you must keep records of the applicable data recorded and calculations performed that you used to determine your affected EGU's gross or net energy output for each operating month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of percentage of valid CO2 mass emission rates
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep records of the calculations you performed to determine the percentage of valid CO2 mass emission rates in each compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of compliance calculations with CO2 mass emissions standards
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep records of the calculations you performed to assess compliance with each applicable CO2 mass emissions standard in table 1 or 2 to this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of site‑specific carbon-based F-factors
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep records of the calculations you performed to determine any site-specific carbon-based F-factors you used in the emissions calculations (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of electric sales for stationary combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: For stationary combustion turbines, you must keep records of electric sales to determine the applicable subcategory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation to demonstrate operation during a system emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep records to demonstrate that your affected facility operated during a system emergency, including documentation that the system emergency was in effect, that the emergency included the affected source/region, and that the facility was instructed to increase output or remain in operation outside scheduled dispatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records required: (1) Documentation of the system emergency from the entity issuing the alert and exact duration; (2) Documentation that the system emergency included the affected source/region; (3) Documentation that the facility was instructed by a Reliability Coordinator, Balancing Authority, or ISO/RTO to increase output beyond planned day-ahead levels and/or remain in operation outside scheduled dispatch during emergency conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and availability of records
rubrics_metrics.description: Your records must be in a form suitable and readily available for expeditious review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period (5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must maintain each record for 5 years after the date of conclusion of each compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-site retention requirement (2 years) and off-site storage
rubrics_metrics.description: You must maintain each record on site for at least 2 years after the date of each occurrence, measurement, maintenance, corrective action, report, or record, according to § 60.7. Records accessible from a central location by a computer or other means that instantly provide access at the site meet this requirement; off-site storage is allowed for the remaining year(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Subpart A (general provisions) to this subpart
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain parts of the general provisions in §§ 60.1 through 60.19, listed in table 3, do or do not apply to affected EGUs under this subpart; where inconsistent, this subpart's requirements apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 3 enumerates which general provisions apply (e.g., § 60.1, § 60.2, § 60.3 apply) and which do not (e.g., § 60.8(a) performance tests not applicable; § 60.13(a)-(h),(j) monitoring requirements not applicable because monitoring is done according to part 75), and notes specific exceptions (e.g., § 60.4 does not apply to information reported electronically through ECMPS). Administrator can approve certain alternatives per § 60.8(b) and § 60.13(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation and enforcement delegation and retained EPA authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart can be implemented and enforced by the EPA, or a delegated authority such as your state, local, or Tribal agency; if delegated, EPA retains certain authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA retains authorities including: (1) approval of alternatives to the emission standards; (2) approval of major alternatives to test methods; (3) approval of major alternatives to monitoring; (4) approval of major alternatives to recordkeeping and reporting; (5) performance test and data reduction waivers under § 60.8(b). Contact EPA Regional Office to determine delegation status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Annual capacity factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the ratio between the actual heat input to an EGU during a calendar year and the potential heat input had it operated for 8,760 hours at the base load rating; actual and potential heat input from non-combustion sources are not included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and criteria: Base load combustion turbine
rubrics_metrics.description: A stationary combustion turbine that supplies more than 40 percent of its potential electric output as net-electric sales on both a 12-operating month and a 3-year rolling average basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Base load rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the maximum amount of heat input (fuel) that an EGU can combust on a steady state basis plus the maximum amount of heat input derived from non-combustion sources, as determined by physical design and characteristics at ISO conditions; for stationary combustion turbines, base load rating includes heat input from duct burners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Design efficiency and acceptable methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Design efficiency means the rated overall net efficiency (e.g., electric plus useful thermal output) on a higher heating value basis at the base load rating, ISO conditions, and maximum useful thermal output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design efficiency shall be determined using one of the following: ASME PTC 22-2014, ASME PTC 46-1996, ISO 2314:2009 (E), or an alternative approved by the Administrator. Output of integrated equipment and energy storage are included when determining design efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Gross energy output (calculation rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross energy output is defined differently by EGU type: (1) For stationary combustion turbines and IGCC: gross electric or direct mechanical output plus 100% of the useful thermal output. (2) For steam generating units: gross electric/mechanical output minus electricity used to power feedwater pumps plus 100% of useful thermal output. (3) For CHP facilities meeting the 20% useful thermal output threshold: formula involving gross electric output, auxiliary loads, and division by 0.95 plus 100% of useful thermal output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Valid data (quality-assured data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Valid data means quality-assured data generated by continuous monitoring systems installed, operated, and maintained according to part 75 of this chapter, meeting initial certification and on-going QA requirements specified in 40 CFR part 75 appendices and sections referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CEMS: meet initial certification in 40 CFR 75.20 and appendix A before reporting; on-going QA per appendix B sections and data validation criteria. For fuel flow meters: meet initial certification and on-going QA per appendix D to 40 CFR part 75 (with exceptions for qualifying commercial billing meters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Violation
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation means a specified averaging period over which the CO2 emissions rate is higher than the applicable emissions standard located in table 1 to this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 emission standards for stationary combustion turbines (Table 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical CO2 emission standards differ by affected EGU category and time period and may be gross- or net-energy output based as approved by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Base load combustion turbines — for 12-operating month averages beginning before Jan 2032: 360–560 kg CO2/MWh (gross) or 370–570 kg CO2/MWh (net); for averages beginning after Dec 2031: 43–67 kg CO2/MWh (gross) or 42–64 kg CO2/MWh (net). Intermediate load: 530–710 kg CO2/MWh (gross) or 540–700 kg CO2/MWh (net). Low load combustion turbines: 50–69 kg CO2/GJ (heat input). (Numerical values presented with stated significant figures conventions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 emission standard for modified coal-fired steam generating unit (Table 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A unit-specific emissions standard determined by an 88.4 percent reduction in the unit's best historical annual CO2 emission rate (from 2002 to the date of the modification).

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan submission requirement (who is affected)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are the Governor of a State in the contiguous U.S. with one or more affected EGUs that must be addressed in your State plan, you must submit a State plan to EPA that implements the emission guidelines; if you have no affected EGUs or all excluded, you must submit a negative declaration letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a coal-fired steam generating unit meets certain conditions to permanently cease before Jan 1, 2032 and would otherwise be an affected EGU, it must comply with § 60.5876b.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA review and approval timeline for State plans
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will determine completeness of a State plan submission according to § 60.27a(g) and will act on the submission according to § 60.27a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator will have 12 months after the final State plan or revision is found complete to fully approve, partially approve, conditionally approve, partially disapprove, and/or fully disapprove such State plan or revision or each portion thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal plan fallback if State plan not submitted or approvable
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State does not submit an approvable State plan, EPA will develop and implement a Federal plan for the State to implement the emission guidelines; owners/operators not covered by an approved State plan must comply with the Federal plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Federal plan will be withdrawn when the State submits and EPA approves a State plan replacing the relevant portion(s) of the Federal plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible alternatives to submitting a State plan
rubrics_metrics.description: A State may meet its CAA section 111(d) obligations only by submitting a State plan or, if applicable, a negative declaration letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative declaration letter process
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no formal EPA review process for negative declaration letters; EPA will place a copy in the public docket and publish a notice in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If at a later date an affected EGU is found in the State that should have been addressed, the State will be treated as having failed to submit a State plan and a Federal plan will apply until a State plan is submitted and approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan required components (identification and subcategorization of affected EGUs)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include identification of affected EGUs covered and all affected EGUs in the State that meet applicability criteria, and must subcategorize affected EGUs into specified subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories include: (i) long-term coal-fired steam generating units (not medium-term and not planning to cease before Jan 1, 2039); (ii) medium-term coal-fired units (commit to permanently cease after Dec 31, 2031 and before Jan 1, 2039); (iii) base load oil-fired (annual capacity factor ≥45%); (iv) intermediate load oil-fired (≥8% and <45%); (v) low load oil-fired (<8%); (vi) base load natural gas-fired (≥45%); (vii) intermediate load natural gas-fired (≥8% and <45%); (viii) low load natural gas-fired (<8%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory of Data from Affected EGUs required in State plan
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include an inventory of specified data from affected EGUs, including nameplate capacity, base load rating, and continuous 5‑year data immediately prior to May 9, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5-year data must include: (A) sum of CO2 emissions during each quarter in the 5-year period; (B) sum of gross energy output each quarter (or heat input for low load subcategories); (C) heat input for each fuel type each quarter; (D) start/end dates and sums for the most representative continuous 8-quarter period used to determine baseline emission performance, including CO2 mass emissions, gross energy output or heat input, and heat input by fuel type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of performance in State plan
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include all standards of performance for each affected EGU according to § 60.5775b, established at a level not exceeding the level calculated through methods in § 60.5775b(b) unless the State establishes a standard pursuant to § 60.5775b(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategory applicability requirements to include in State plan
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include enforceable requirements to establish an affected EGU's applicability for each subcategory (e.g., permanent cessation dates, coal capability removal, fuel usage estimates, shutdown procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) Medium-term coal-fired units must permanently cease operations by a date after Dec 31, 2031 and before Jan 1, 2039. (B) Steam units that retain capability to fire coal and meet certain historical conditions must remove the capability to fire coal before Jan 1, 2030. (C) For each affected EGU estimate coal/oil/natural gas usage by heat input for the first 3 calendar years after Jan 1, 2030. (D) Units planning to permanently cease must comply with State and Federal requirements for permanent cessation, including removal from State emission inventories and amending/revoking permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increments of progress and enforceable deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include legally enforceable increments of progress as required elements for affected EGUs in long-term and medium-term coal-fired subcategories, with calendar-date deadlines and reporting obligations where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For long-term coal-fired units using carbon capture and medium-term units using natural gas co‑firing to meet standards, State plans must assign deadlines to each increment of progress and meet website reporting obligations. Example increment: submittal of a final control plan to the appropriate air pollution control agency (further increments continue in the regulation).
